theory.intro: When a quantity $Q$ changes over time $t$, $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}$ is its rate of change at that instant. A positive rate means $Q$ is rising, a negative rate means it is falling. $\dfrac{d^{2}Q}{dt^{2}}$ tells you how the rate itself is changing.
facts: $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}$ has the units of $Q$ divided by the units of $t$, such as litres per minute.
$Q(a)$ is how much there is at time $a$, while $Q'(a)$ is how fast it is changing then.
A negative rate means the quantity is **decreasing**, and the size of the rate says how fast.
Solving $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=0$ finds the times when the quantity is momentarily neither rising nor falling.
$\dfrac{d^{2}Q}{dt^{2}}$ is the rate of change of the rate, in units of $Q$ per unit time squared.
If $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}<0$ and $\dfrac{d^{2}Q}{dt^{2}}>0$, the quantity is falling but the fall is slowing.
Setting $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}$ equal to a given rate and solving gives the time when that rate occurs.
$\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=0$ with $\dfrac{d^{2}Q}{dt^{2}}<0$ marks a local maximum of $Q$, and $\dfrac{d^{2}Q}{dt^{2}}>0$ marks a local minimum.
steps: Write the quantity $Q$ as a function of time $t$, noting the units of each.
Differentiate to get $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}$, and differentiate again for $\dfrac{d^{2}Q}{dt^{2}}$ if needed.
Substitute the given time, or set the derivative equal to the required rate and solve.
State the answer with its units and say whether the quantity is increasing or decreasing.

workedExamples.question_text: A reservoir contains $Q=160+18t-2t^{2}$ megalitres after $t$ days, for $0\le t\le 8$. Find the amount of water and its instantaneous rate of change at $t=3$ days. Interpret the rate.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}Q(3)&=160+18(3)-2(3^{2})\\&=196\text{ ML}\end{align*}$
Differentiate to find the rate.
$\begin{align*}Q'(t)&=18-4t\\Q'(3)&=18-4(3)\\&=6\text{ ML/day}\end{align*}$
The reservoir contains $196$ megalitres and is filling at $6$ megalitres per day.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) A tank contains $V=420-\dfrac{96}{t+2}$ litres after $t$ hours, for $t\ge0$. Find its filling rate at $t=2$ hours.
(b) A cyclist's distance travelled is $d=12\sqrt{t}+2t$ metres after $t$ seconds, for $t\ge0$. Find the speed at $t=9$ seconds.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Write the reciprocal as a negative power.
$\begin{align*}V&=420-96(t+2)^{-1}\\V'(t)&=96(t+2)^{-2}\\V'(2)&=\frac{96}{4^{2}}\\&=6\text{ L/h}\end{align*}$
The tank is filling at $6$ litres per hour.
(b) Write the square root as a fractional power.
$\begin{align*}d&=12t^{1/2}+2t\\d'(t)&=6t^{-1/2}+2\\d'(9)&=\frac{6}{\sqrt{9}}+2\\&=4\text{ m/s}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A liquid drains from a tank whose volume is $V=240-8t-t^{2}$ litres after $t$ minutes, for $0\le t\le10$. When is the volume decreasing at $20$ litres per minute?
workedExamples.solution_text:
A decrease of $20$ litres per minute means $V'(t)=-20$.
$\begin{align*}V'(t)&=-8-2t\\-8-2t&=-20\\2t&=12\\t&=6\text{ min}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: The mass of a substance is $M=t^{3}-9t^{2}+24t+20$ grams after $t$ hours, for $0\le t\le6$. Find when the mass is momentarily stationary and classify each stationary value as a local maximum or local minimum.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The mass is stationary when $M'(t)=0$.
$\begin{align*}M'(t)&=3t^{2}-18t+24\\3t^{2}-18t+24&=0\\t^{2}-6t+8&=0\\(t-2)(t-4)&=0\\t&=2\text{ or }4\end{align*}$
Use the second derivative to classify these times.
$\begin{align*}M''(t)&=6t-18\\M''(2)&=-6<0\\M''(4)&=6>0\end{align*}$
The mass has a local maximum at $t=2$ hours and a local minimum at $t=4$ hours.

workedExamples.question_text: A tank contains $Q=120-18t+2t^{2}$ litres after $t$ hours, for $0\le t\le4$. Find $Q'(2)$ and $Q''(2)$, including their units. Explain what both values tell you about the water.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}Q'(t)&=-18+4t\\Q'(2)&=-10\text{ L/h}\\Q''(t)&=4\\Q''(2)&=4\text{ L/h}^{2}\end{align*}$
The volume is falling at $10$ litres per hour. The positive second derivative means the net rate is increasing; the rate of fall is slowing.

workedExamples.question_text: The volume of water in a tank is $V=20+18t^{2}-t^{3}$ litres after $t$ hours, for $0\le t\le12$. Find when the volume is increasing most rapidly and determine that rate.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Let $R(t)=V'(t)$ be the net filling rate.
$\begin{align*}R(t)&=36t-3t^{2}\\R'(t)&=V''(t)=36-6t\\36-6t&=0\\t&=6\end{align*}$
For $0<t<6$, $R'(t)>0$; for $6<t<12$, $R'(t)<0$. The rate increases then decreases, so its maximum occurs at $t=6$ hours.
$\begin{align*}R(0)&=0\\R(6)&=36(6)-3(6^{2})\\&=108\text{ L/h}\\R(12)&=0\end{align*}$
The greatest filling rate is $108$ litres per hour at $t=6$ hours.

workedExamples.question_text: The mass of chemical present is $Q=15t^{2}-t^{3}$ grams after $t$ minutes, for $0\le t\le15$. Find when the mass is increasing while its net production rate is decreasing.
workedExamples.solution_text:
An increasing mass requires $Q'(t)>0$.
$\begin{align*}Q'(t)&=30t-3t^{2}\\&=3t(10-t)\end{align*}$
Thus $Q'(t)>0$ for $0<t<10$.
A decreasing net production rate requires $Q''(t)<0$.
$\begin{align*}Q''(t)&=30-6t\\30-6t&<0\\t&>5\end{align*}$
Both conditions hold for $5<t<10$ minutes.

workedExamples.question_text:
A metal plate has temperature $T=18+80e^{-0.2t}$ degrees Celsius after $t$ minutes, for $t\ge0$.
(a) Find its temperature and instantaneous rate of change at $t=5$ minutes, each to $1$ decimal place.
(b) Find when it is cooling at $4$ degrees Celsius per minute, to $1$ decimal place.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a)
$\begin{align*}T(5)&=18+80e^{-1}\\&\approx47.4^{\circ}\text{C}\\T'(t)&=80(-0.2)e^{-0.2t}\\&=-16e^{-0.2t}\\T'(5)&=-16e^{-1}\\&\approx-5.9^{\circ}\text{C/min}\end{align*}$
The plate is cooling at $5.9$ degrees Celsius per minute.
(b) Cooling at $4$ degrees Celsius per minute means $T'(t)=-4$.
$\begin{align*}-16e^{-0.2t}&=-4\\e^{-0.2t}&=\frac14\\-0.2t&=\ln\left(\frac14\right)\\t&=\frac{\ln(1/4)}{-0.2}\\&\approx6.9\text{ min}\end{align*}$

foundation.question_text:
A tank holds $V=3t^{2}+8t$ litres of water after $t$ minutes.
Find the rate at which the volume is increasing when $t=5$ minutes.

A block of ice has mass $M=90-4t^{2}$ grams after $t$ hours.
Find $\dfrac{dM}{dt}$ when $t=3$ hours and say what it means.
foundation.solution_text:
$M=90-4t^{2}$
$\dfrac{dM}{dt}=-8t$
$\text{At }t=3:$
$\dfrac{dM}{dt}=-8(3)$
$=-24\text{ g/h}$
The mass is decreasing at $24$ grams per hour.

foundation.question_text:
A dam holds $Q=200+15t-t^{2}$ megalitres after $t$ days.
Find the amount of water at $t=4$ days, and the rate at which it is changing at that time.

A ball is thrown so its height is $h=24t-3t^{2}$ metres after $t$ seconds.
Find the time when the height is momentarily not changing.

A cup of coffee has temperature $T$ degrees Celsius after $t$ minutes.
At $t=10$ minutes, $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-2.5$.
Describe what is happening to the temperature.
foundation.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-2.5$
The rate is negative, so the temperature is falling.
The coffee is cooling at $2.5$ degrees Celsius per minute at $t=10$ minutes.

foundation.question_text:
A quantity is given by $Q=2t^{3}-5t^{2}+7t$ litres after $t$ hours.
Find $\dfrac{d^{2}Q}{dt^{2}}$ when $t=2$ hours.

The volume of gas in a cylinder is $V=2t^{2}+5t$ cubic centimetres after $t$ seconds.
Find the time at which the volume is increasing at $37\text{ cm}^{3}\text{/s}$.

development.question_text:
A reservoir holds $V=500-\dfrac{100}{t+1}$ litres after $t$ hours.
Find the rate at which it is filling when $t=4$ hours.

A bacterial culture has population $P=t^{3}-12t^{2}+36t$ thousand after $t$ hours.
Find the times at which the population is momentarily stationary.

Water flows into and out of a tank. Its volume is $Q=100+4t^{3}-30t^{2}+48t$ litres after $t$ minutes, for $0\le t\le 5$.
Find the time at which the net flow rate $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}$ is a minimum.
development.solution_text:
$Q=100+4t^{3}-30t^{2}+48t$
$\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=12t^{2}-60t+48$
$\dfrac{d^{2}Q}{dt^{2}}=24t-60$
$24t-60=0$
$t=2.5$
$\dfrac{d^{2}Q}{dt^{2}}$ changes from negative to positive, so the net flow rate is least at $t=2.5$ minutes.

development.question_text:
For a tank of water, $\dfrac{dV}{dt}=0$ and $\dfrac{d^{2}V}{dt^{2}}=3$ when $t=6$ hours.
What does this tell you about the volume at $t=6$ hours?
development.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dV}{dt}=0$, so the volume is momentarily neither rising nor falling.
$\dfrac{d^{2}V}{dt^{2}}=3>0$, so the rate is increasing through zero.
The volume is at a local minimum at $t=6$ hours.

development.question_text:
A metal plate cools so that $T=20+60e^{-0.5t}$ degrees Celsius after $t$ minutes.
Find the temperature and the rate of cooling when $t=2$ minutes, each to $1$ decimal place.
development.solution_text:
$T=20+60e^{-0.5t}$
$T(2)=20+60e^{-1}$
$=20+22.0728\ldots$
$=42.1^{\circ}\text{C}$
$\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-30e^{-0.5t}$
$\text{At }t=2:$
$\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-30e^{-1}$
$=-11.0^{\circ}\text{C/min}$
The plate is cooling at $11.0$ degrees Celsius per minute.

Find the speed $\dfrac{dd}{dt}$ when $t=4$ seconds.

A liquid drains so that $V=180-6t-t^{2}$ litres after $t$ minutes.
Find the time at which the volume is decreasing at $16$ litres per minute.

mastery.question_text:
The mass of chemical present is $Q=12t^{2}-t^{3}$ grams after $t$ minutes, for $0\le t\le 12$. Its net production rate is $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}$.
Find the interval of time during which $Q$ is increasing but the net production rate is decreasing.

Water is pumped into a storage tank so that the volume of water after $t$ hours is $V=27t^{2}-t^{3}$ litres, for $0\le t\le 18$.
Find the time at which the volume is increasing at the greatest rate, and determine this maximum rate.
mastery.solution_text:
$V=27t^{2}-t^{3}$
$\dfrac{dV}{dt}=54t-3t^{2}$
$\dfrac{d^{2}V}{dt^{2}}=54-6t$
$54-6t=0$
$6t=54$
$t=9\text{ h}$
$\dfrac{d^{2}V}{dt^{2}}>0\text{ for }t<9\text{ and }\dfrac{d^{2}V}{dt^{2}}<0\text{ for }t>9$, so the rate of increase is a maximum.
$\text{At }t=9:$
$\dfrac{dV}{dt}=54(9)-3(9^{2})$
$=486-243$
$=243\text{ L/h}$
The volume is increasing most rapidly at $t=9$ hours, at a rate of $243$ litres per hour.

mastery.question_text:

Find, to $1$ decimal place, the time at which the rod is cooling at $6$ degrees Celsius per minute.
